title: Agency Rights (LIC)
summary: Adults who meet LIC's basic onboarding criteria can work as agents and pursue self-employment through insurance distribution.
benefit: Supports flexible work, income generation, and professional autonomy.

title: Hereditary Commission
summary: Renewal commissions attached to eligible LIC agency work can continue in favor of legal heirs under the applicable agency framework.
benefit: Adds a family-security dimension to long-term agency work.

title: Agency Perks and Advances
summary: Eligible LIC agents may access benefits such as interest-free advances, insurance-linked support, and agency-related perks subject to policy conditions.
benefit: Can reduce the setup burden for agents building a practice.

title: Free Look Period for Life Insurance
summary: Policyholders generally get a post-receipt review window to examine a life insurance policy and exit under the insurer's free-look rules if they disagree with the terms.
benefit: Helps consumers avoid staying locked into an unsuitable policy without review.

title: Mukhyamantri Yojana Doot Opportunity
summary: A Maharashtra opportunity aimed at outreach and awareness work related to welfare programmes at the grassroots level.
benefit: Relevant for young applicants looking for state-linked public outreach work.

title: Yojana Doot Eligibility Rights
summary: The current seed entry reflects the age, residency, device, and education expectations described on the existing rights page for Yojana Doot applicants.
benefit: Makes it easier to pre-check whether the role is worth exploring before opening the official portal.

title: Yojana Doot Application Guidance
summary: This seed right captures the current rights-page guidance that the application flow is online and document-driven.
benefit: Useful for turning static legal-awareness content into a filterable, action-oriented record.

title: Yojana Doot Contract Transparency
summary: The current rights-page content notes that the role is fixed-term and should be understood as a temporary opportunity rather than a permanent government appointment.
benefit: Helps applicants calibrate expectations before applying.
